blind_spots.blind_spot: Vision-based ML inference is the single hardest thing to space-qualify, and nothing in their language addresses radiation tolerance or flight qualification of the compute
blind_spots.operator_reality: A defense bus integrator will ask for the part number of the processor, its total-ionizing-dose and single-event-upset data, and the flight-software qualification evidence for the neural net running on it. 'Turn pixels into reliable actions on orbit' on COTS edge silicon is where a NASA study contract stops and a defense program starts — and a non-deterministic model in the GNC loop has no accepted qualification precedent to point at.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: The heritage is a university rendezvous lab where the hard problem was the algorithm, and the flight demonstrations were research missions with research risk postures.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: EraDrive provides full stack onboard autonomy modules that turn pixels from space-based sensors into reliable actions on orbit

blind_spots.blind_spot: The business model depends on an offboard 'real-time, space-wide traffic intelligence network' fed by downlink — a bandwidth assumption a contested or ground-station-limited mission denies
blind_spots.operator_reality: A LEO spacecraft gets minutes of contact per pass, and a defense mission may deliberately go quiet. If the value story is a live traffic picture aggregated on the ground, the product degrades to nothing exactly when the contested-orbit scenario they sell against occurs. The architecture fix is the same one as the 30fps case: decouple onboard action from the offboard feed, compress observations into event summaries sized to a pass, and prove the module is fully useful with zero downlink.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: The data-network flywheel is the venture story on top of the module sale; commercial SDA customers have routine ground contact, so the denied case never had to be designed for.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Our dual-use platform serves both commercial and government missions, while simultaneously collecting critical data to power a real-time, space-wide traffic intelligence network.

blind_spots.blind_spot: No export-control or security posture anywhere, while selling autonomy modules for 'military applications' and hiring PhD-heavy engineering in Palo Alto
blind_spots.operator_reality: Spacecraft GNC and RPO software is squarely ITAR/USML territory. Export control determines who may touch the repo, whether a foreign-national researcher can be hired, how a technical data package moves to a prime, and whether a facility clearance or CMMC posture is needed before a defense subcontract can flow down. For a Stanford spinoff whose talent pool is disproportionately international, this is a hiring constraint that arrives as a surprise mid-program.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: The first contract was NASA civil space, which imposes far lighter export and personnel constraints than a DoD RPO program.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: AI-powered vision to navigate, operate, and collaborate in space for commercial and military applications

opener_hook: SpaceNews reported EraDrive's first contract, $1M from NASA, in July 2025 — and your site's proof point is 12 satellites flown over 23 years, which is SLAB's flight record rather than the company's, a distinction a defense program office will make when it asks for qualification evidence on the compute your vision stack runs on.
what_they_do: Stanford spinoff building compact onboard autonomy modules (vision-based navigation, collision avoidance, rendezvous) for spacecraft, plus a ground-side space-traffic data layer.
